# requirePresentation

<link-summary>Returns the value as a presentation, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requirePresentation() — Returns the value as a presentation, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/slide</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requirePresentation(
  value: unknown,
  message: string = "Required Presentation object is missing or invalid."
): GoogleAppsScript.Slides.Presentation;
```

An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard looks for the methods that define the type — `getId`, `getSlides`. A stub that implements them passes, which is what makes code using this guard testable outside the runtime.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                                        | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                                          | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Required Presentation object is missing or invalid."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`GoogleAppsScript.Slides.Presentation` — the same value, typed as a presentation.

## Throws

| Exception                      | Condition                        |
| :----------------------------- | :------------------------------- |
| `InvalidPresentationException` | the value is not a presentation. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
const presentation = SlidesApp.getActivePresentation();

requirePresentation(presentation); // => presentation
requirePresentation({}); // throws InvalidPresentationException
requirePresentation(null); // throws InvalidPresentationException
```
